queue.mechanism: redundant per-opening recomputation plus a repeated FFI bound-submission crossing for an opening-invariant column-bound pin and an opening-invariant commitment relaxation
queue.claim: For a Generated child run carrying more than one opening, the per-opening backward prep redundantly re-fills and re-submits the opening-invariant column-bound state pin from the unchanged x_hat and col_scale, costing one fill over n_state plus one set_col_bounds per opening that the CLP backend expands into a full-length col_lower and col_upper FFI push; the opening-invariant commitment relaxation is additionally re-filled per opening only when n_anticipated is nonzero and the stage has geometry, and re-submitted only when the relaxation set is nonempty. The claim is redundant call frequency alone: no pinned contract is violated, patch.rs's 'once per stage-visit' rustdoc is a value-semantics contract the current code already satisfies, and the External single-opening branch carries no redundancy.
queue.byteNeutralFixShape: Hoist the opening-invariant work to per-child: fill and submit the column-bound state pin (fill_col_state_patches plus its set_col_bounds) and fill the commitment relaxation once alongside load_backward_lp, and narrow the per-opening entry point to what actually varies -- the row patches from the transformed inflow/load noise and the NCS availability column patch. All three backward drivers reach this through the single helper patch_opening_bounds, so the blast radius is that helper plus a parameterization of StageSolvePrep::run (a per-child prep and a per-opening prep), with no driver-by-driver edit. Three pinned contracts govern it. .claude/rules/sddp.md Sec. State pinning uses column bounds, not equality rows: the pin stays a column-bound pin at the same incoming columns and merely recovers the once-per-stage-visit identity patch.rs's rustdoc already declares. Sec. Lower-bound evaluation must patch NCS: the NCS patch stays per opening and must not be hoisted with it. And the ordering rule reconcile_commitments carries in its rustdoc -- it runs last because the template reload and the bound patches reset the columns it relaxes -- so the hoist is valid only if the hoisted relaxation still runs after every column submission that touches the anticipated columns it relaxes; at the pin the sole remaining per-opening column submission is the NCS patch, which addresses a different column family, and the fix must verify that disjointness rather than assume it. Byte-neutrality is asserted on the data and validated, not assumed on the solver: every bound value and index in force before each solve is unchanged, but the NUMBER of set_col_bounds calls the solver sees per opening changes, which is the same class of perturbation Sec. Backward opening order is warm-start-only describes for the warm-start chain (a differently-warmed solve may settle on a different-but-equally-valid vertex at a degenerate optimum, the divergence the Cobre determinism contract permits). The fix is therefore gated on the parity goldens (tests/parity.rs, tests/common/parity_hash.rs), the rank-invariance harness (tests/common/permute.rs) and mpiexec -n 1 vs -n 2, plus the opening_order_determinism gate in tests/mpi_wire.rs; if a golden moves, the baseline is the arbiter and the hoist is reconsidered, not rebaselined.
